title.narrative: East Africa Integrated Community HIV and AIDS Programme: DACHEP Administrative costs

description.narrative:
Dar-es-Salaam Archdiocese Community Health Education Programme (DACHEP) and /Pastoral Activities and Services for people with AIDS in Dar-es-Salaam Archdiocese (PASADA) {thus DACHEP/PASADA} have been in partnership with CAFOD since 2004. DACHEP/PASADA implemented the successful joint programme funded by Comic Relief (October 2004 – September 2007) to Strengthen community responses to HIV and AIDS in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. DACHEP/PASADA aims to provide education on health and HIV and AIDS as well as offer comprehensive prevention and support services to people living with HIV and AIDS and affected families. They have an extensive community-based outreach network that directly impacts the daily lives of adults and children infected and affected by HIV and AIDS. The current DACHEP/PASADA project titled ‘East Africa Integrated Community HIV and AIDS Programme' primarily focuses on provision of HIV prevention services that are directly linked with PADASA’s home based care services for PLWHA.
During this implementation period DP made good progress. The project has demonstrated results such as strengthened community capacity, behaviour change via Stepping Stones training and extensive network of volunteers providing services to project beneficiaries. The number of people who seek testing for HIV and know their HIV status and thus access treatment, counselling for positive living, and seek care and support services promptly has increased. It also increased the number of PLWHA empowered and contributing to HIV and AIDS programmes; increased the number of PLWHA with regained self esteem and capacity to take charge of their own lives and increased the number of community members who are knowledgeable about HIV prevention, limiting re-infection, treatment options and positive living. There is evidence of stronger local organisations such as the church (different faiths) taking forward more efficient and effective initiatives for PLWHA and OVC in need through a focused capacity building and shared learning.
This appraisal aims to support DACHEPwho is the key implementing partner in the DACHEP/PASADA project. The grant will support DACHEP’s core cost including staff salaries directly related to the delivery of DACHEP/PASADA project.
